chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu al-Maghra', from Harun ibn Kharaja, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of Allah used to eat the eating of a slave, and sit the sitting of a slave, and he knew that he was a slave.
ai.seo_question: How did the Prophet Muhammad demonstrate humility in his daily habits?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) emphasizes the Prophet’s (PBUH) conscious awareness of his status as a servant ('abd) through his simple eating and sitting habits, contrasting with the arrogance of kings. This aligns with the Shia scholarly understanding that prophetic humility is a manifestation of true servitude to Allah, serving as a practical model for believers to avoid ostentation in daily conduct.
